what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a cryptographic technique that lets a server do computations on data that remains encrypted the entire time — meaning a cloud provider could process your private data without ever seeing it in plain form. FHE is extremely compute-heavy, but it turns out the bottleneck on GPUs is not the complex math operations (like the NTT — Number-Theoretic Transform, a specialized version of the Fourier transform used in FHE) but rather the simpler element-wise operations (adding or multiplying each number in a huge array individually) that saturate the connection between the GPU and its off-chip memory. Anaheim addresses this by placing small computing circuits directly inside the memory chips (processing-in-memory, or PIM), so the simple element-wise operations happen where the data already lives without crossing the slow data bus. The GPU continues handling the complex NTT phases, and a software framework coordinates which chip handles which part of the computation. This is based on the abstract only.
